extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers interested in international/diplomatic affairs (historical)
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting and summarizing international diplomatic, military, and political events (speeches, protests, border clashes), providing context, primary texts, reactions, and on-the-ground details for a general readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish primary-source texts
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper publishes the complete text of important statements (e.g., 'The complete text of Premier Edouard Daladier's radio address tonight follows').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including full texts of speeches or official notes (and indicating intent to publish counterpart documents such as the Italian note of Dec. 17 and the French reply) allows readers to see facts directly and reduces reliance on paraphrase or rumor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report precise broadcast details
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the exact time and medium of major broadcasts (e.g., 'began reading his speech exactly at 7:45 P. M. (2:45 P. M., Eastern standard time)'; note relay languages and territories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Giving precise times, durations, languages and relay scope (French, Italian, German, English, Spanish, Arabic; broadcast throughout France and North African possessions) grounds the report in verifiable details and conveys the intended audience and reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe delivery and tone of speeches
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how a speech was delivered and its emotional content (e.g., 'His voice rose to a shout three times during his speech', 'In slow and measured tones he began').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting on tone, pauses, shouts, and delivery helps readers interpret the speaker's emphasis and intent beyond literal words; include concrete examples (times of raised voice, pauses before names) rather than vague adjectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide historical and diplomatic background
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply background context on prior treaties, notes and actions needed to interpret current events (e.g., references to the 1935 accords, the Dec. 17 Italian note, conquest of Ethiopia, prior recognition and ambassadorial appointments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextual history (treaty dates, prior government actions, contested colonial issues) is essential to understand stakes and to explain why present statements matter; cite specific past acts and dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include international and domestic reactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Report reactions from other governments, domestic bodies and the press (e.g., Britain welcomed the speech, summaries of Berlin press reaction, notes on reactions in Rome and parliamentary preparation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather and summarize responses from relevant states, official spokespeople, and major newspapers to show the diplomatic effect and likely next steps; differentiate official government responses from press commentary or partisan reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribute and qualify rumors and unverified reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Flag and qualify unconfirmed reports (e.g., 'sources of reports, apparently false, that German troops were about to march into Yugoslavia'; 'reports that Chancellor Hitler had decided to convert Memel into a first-class naval base reached here').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label rumors as such, indicate source reliability, and avoid presenting unverified claims as fact; note when reports are 'apparently false' or 'reached here' to indicate distance from primary verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report on on-the-ground incidents with concrete details
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe local demonstrations, expulsions, clashes and their specifics (e.g., pro-German demonstrations in Apace with songs and flags; Danish Ministry of Justice ordered expulsion of three Nazi youths for posting propaganda bills; Slovak-Hungarian fighting near Bunkos village).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the who/what/where/when (locations, numbers, actions taken, casualties or property damage) for local incidents; include official responses or orders where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use direct quotations from officials and documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Quote officials and official statements verbatim (e.g., Daladier's repeated lines: 'we will not cede a foot of our territory and not one of our rights', 'Faithful to the accords she signed in 1935...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct quotes supply authoritative wording, reduce misinterpretation, and let readers judge tone and content; when quoting, provide attribution and situational context (who spoke, where, and why).
